caption:
18 days until the August SAT.

Every quadratic question asks for one of four things: the zeros, the maximum, the minimum, or where it meets a line. Click the curve and Desmos marks all four for you — no factoring, no completing the square, no quadratic formula.

Save this one — it's the whole topic in one place. Seva's practice tests have the same calculator built in, so you can drill these until they're reflex. Free trial — link in bio.

slides.title: Everything Desmos does for ==quadratics==
slides.badge: Zeros, max, min, systems — one screen each

slides.title: Type it in standard form, then click the curve
slides.tip: Desmos marks both roots as grey dots. Click one and it shows (2, 0) — you never factored anything.

slides.title: The peak is a point Desmos already knows
slides.tip: Click the top of the curve for (2, 11). No -b/2a, and no completing the square to get there.

slides.title: Ugly numbers don't make it harder
slides.tip: The minimum always sits halfway between the zeros — here, halfway between -7 and 3.

slides.title: A quadratic and a line cross twice
slides.tip: Graph both and click each crossing. Two crossings means two solutions to the system.
